decisionsTitle: The shared card is a brand card, drawn from a design object the club will be able to change
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01:** «poza descărcată pentru Instagram trebuie să fie un pic mai frumoasă, și pe viitor configurabilă» — the picture downloaded for Instagram should be a little prettier, and configurable later.

**What was there.** Since §90 every event has a card drawn on the server from its own facts: the 1200×630 picture Facebook, WhatsApp and every link preview show, and the same card as a square for Instagram, which takes no link. §90 chose facts over a photograph on purpose — an event has no cover picture, and a card that says when and where is what a runner wants from a share. §140 made the square a button called «Instagram», and §299 made that button hand the picture to the phone's own share sheet where it can. The card itself had not changed since §90: a flat diagonal blue, the club's name in spaced capitals behind a small orange bar, a translucent pill with the event's type, the title, «Sâmbătă, 21 nov. 2026 · 10:00» on one line, the place, the distance and the climb with orange dots between them, and the site's address. Correct, and plain: no logo, and nothing told the eye where to look first except the size of the title.

**What changes, in what a person sees** (`events/share-image.tsx`):

- *The club's own logo* at the top left — the white lockup, mountains and «BRASOV RUNNERS», the same file the race numbers carry — instead of the name typed out, 150 pixels tall on the square and 100 on the wide card: the square is seen at about 400 pixels wide on a phone, where a 100-pixel lockup left its wordmark about 14 pixels high and the brand on Instagram is the point of the picture. The type pill is centred on the logo's height. The name is therefore the artwork's letters: `CLUB_NAME` is no longer typed onto the card, and a card with the logo switched off carries no name, only the address in the band (the criteria that read the club's name from `CLUB_NAME`, BR-REQ-052-02 11 and BR-REQ-053-01 15 (§357, §369), are both amended to say so).
- *A background with depth*: the same blue diagonal, a soft light at the top right, and one large circle of the kit's orange, faint, half off the bottom-right corner. Nothing busier: no pattern, no stripes, no stock photograph.
- *A hierarchy*: the type pill is a quiet tint of the words' colour with a thin line round it, so that the one solid orange pill on the card is the cancelled one's; the title is larger, at most three lines, under it a short orange rule; then the date with **the time as the headline** — the day in regular weight and the hour large and bold beside it, an orange dot between; the meeting point with a pin; the distance and the climb as two rounded chips, each with a small drawing (a route, a mountain).
- *A white band at the foot* with the site's address in the club's blue and the club's mountains at its right — the site's address is what turns a saved picture back into a visit.
- *Optional, and off by default*: a short line in the club's handwriting face under the title (a tagline), and a photograph behind everything under a blue veil that keeps the words legible — on any photograph, a near-white one included: the veil holds 0.72 of the base colour over the top quarter, behind the logo and the pill (white reads there at about 5:1 over pure white), eases to 0.6 at the middle, where the title is large and the photograph shows most, and deepens to 0.88 at the foot behind the facts; over a photograph the radial light is left off and the type pill is a shade of the blue rather than a tint of white, both of which would lighten the corner the pill sits in. At a quarter of the base, as first written, the white logo and pill over a pale photograph read at about 1.5:1.

A cancelled event keeps what it had on the old card — always, even with the type switched off, because a cancellation is a fact the card must state, not a label the club may hide — the pill that is solid orange with the word «Anulat» (dark letters on the kit's orange, white on a dark accent the club may choose later) while a scheduled event's pill is only a tint — the colour says it before the word is read, and a test holds the two apart; a date, a time or a place not yet announced says so in the same words as before (§328, §533), and only an announced time becomes the headline.

**The design object, and why it exists before anything stores it** (`events/share-card-design.ts`). «Pe viitor configurabilă» is a promise about later, and the cheapest way to keep it is to make the drawing take every decision from one place now. `ShareCardDesign` holds them: the look (`brand` — the blue, the default; `ink` — near-black with a blue glow; `paper` — the page's off-white with dark words and a blue band), the accent colour (the kit's orange), whether the logo, the type, the place, the route and the address are drawn, the tagline (at most 60 characters) and the background picture (an absolute `https:` address, or none). `readShareCardDesign` reads anything — an old row, a typo, garbage — as a design, field by field, and never throws: a card that fails to draw is worse than a plain card, the reasoning of the race number's design (§249). Every element that can be switched off leaves no gap behind it. Today nothing stores the object and every caller passes the platform's defaults. **The next step, named and not built:** a `share_card_design` JSON column on `events`, read through `readShareCardDesign`, and a box in the event editor beside the race number's — exactly the pair `bib_design` is (§249) — when the club asks for it. A picture address is `https:` only and nothing narrower for now; limiting it to the pictures this site stored, as the bibs do, belongs with that box and is recommended there — today nothing stores an address at all. `eventShareImage` runs whatever design it is handed through `readShareCardDesign` before drawing, so a caller that one day hands it a stored design cannot skip those rules, and the renderer itself fetches `https:` only and takes no `data:` address.

**What Satori decided.** `next/og` draws through Satori, which lays out with flexbox only, wants every element with children set to `display: flex`, and draws every line of text it is given — it never shrinks a text to fit, so a title, a place or a tagline that runs long pushes what is under it, the band included, off the card's foot. The review measured exactly that on the wide card: a three-line title with a place that wrapped to a second line left a 66-pixel band of 80, and a tagline beside a long title 69. So the card is laid out before it is drawn (`events/share-card-layout.ts`, pure). Each letter's width is Roboto's own advance, measured once from the bundled files and kept as a table (the wider of the regular and the bold, so neither weight is ever narrower than it says); `lineCount` wraps a text at its spaces the way Satori does, line by line (`textWrap: balance` evens the lines without adding one); `titleRoom` adds up, from the same numbers the drawing uses, the height of everything on the card but the title — the paddings, the band, the logo's row, the rule and the tagline, the date line, the place, the chips (and whether they wrap to a second row) — each only when it is drawn; and `shareTitleSize` picks the largest size whose lines, three at most, fit what is left. On the square that is about 375 pixels with the platform's card, so a title is drawn at 92 pixels up to about sixty characters and a sentence-case title of 85, 100 and 110 characters at 64, 56 and 50 — never smaller than the date line beside it, which it was at 44 when the room was guessed at 300; an all-capitals title of 110 goes to 40 to stay on three lines. On the wide card the same arithmetic within its 630 pixels: two lines from about 50 pixels up, and a tagline beside the rule takes its line from the title's room, so the title steps down rather than the band. The place is cut by length, at a word, with «…» (`clampPlace`, sixty characters), and shorter still while it is wider than its line beside the pin — the square's larger letters hold fewer — and drawn `nowrap` with an ellipsis as the last guard; the title is cut past 110 characters the same way (`clampTitle`). Should the arithmetic ever be wrong, the facts' column clips what overflows rather than move the band. The logo and the mountains are handed over as data, read once per process (and named in `outputFileTracingIncludes` for the two routes, so the build ships them); a read that fails is not remembered, so one transient error at a cold start does not draw every card of that instance without the club's identity — the next card reads again, and the handwriting face the same. When it cannot be read, the tagline is drawn in Roboto and the layout budgets its lines in Roboto's wider letters, so the title steps down rather than the band moving. A tagline is balanced like the title, so a sentence on the square does not end on an orphaned word. A background picture is fetched on each render, behind the route's hour-long cache, at an `https:` address only, without following a redirect, with a five-second deadline and a four-megabyte ceiling checked on the announced length first and again while the body is read, and anything that fails draws the card without it, the unread body of a refused answer cancelled. The chips keep the long words, «circa 10 km» and «350 m diferență de nivel» (§585, §598), not the pill's «≈ 10 km»: the bundled Roboto has no «≈», a missing letter makes Satori download a font from Google in the middle of drawing, and re-subsetting the font for one sign is not worth what it would add to every card. The handwriting face (Caveat, already in the repository for the signed declaration) is loaded only for a card that has a tagline (and if the file cannot be read the tagline is drawn in Roboto), because Satori parses every font it is handed and the file is six times Roboto's.

The site's own card (`[locale]/opengraph-image.tsx`) shares no code with the event's and is unchanged.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/events/share-card-design.test.ts` — the defaults, garbage read as the defaults, a bad accent read as the orange, a `javascript:`, `http:` or `data:` picture read as none, each palette accepted, the tagline cut at its ceiling, the colours of each palette and of a picture (no light, the pill a shade of the base), the veil's three stops giving white 4.5:1 at the top and the foot and 3:1 at the middle over pure white, the pill letters on a light and a dark accent, the title's and the place's clamps. `tests/unit/events/share-card-layout.test.ts` — the measured widths, the wrap, the chips' rows, the title's size never growing with its length, a sentence-case title of 85 to 110 characters at 50 pixels or more on the square, and, for the review's cases on both shapes (a 110-character title with a 93-character place, a long title with a sixty-character tagline, both at once, the date held back, nothing but the facts), the title's lines at its size within three and within the room; the place cut at a word to what its line holds. `tests/unit/events/share-image.test.ts` — the real `next/og` drawing both shapes to a PNG whose header says 1080×1080 and 1200×630, with every element switched off, for a cancelled event and for a date and place to be announced, over a background picture, in the ink and paper looks and with a tagline; the PNG's own pixels read back through `sharp` for the review's cases and an all-capitals one, on both shapes: the paper band fills exactly its last 104 rows on the square and 80 on the wide card, and the logo stands where the plain card has it (an overflow, clipped, would push it up — the test fails when the title is not sized by its room); a near-white photograph, served like every picture through a stub of `fetch` at an `https:` address, leaves 4.5:1 for white behind the wordmark and the pill; a `data:` address is drawn as the plain card without a request, and so is a picture announcing more than four megabytes. The existing tests of the picture's words (§328, §349) pass unchanged.

*Rejected:* a photograph picked automatically from the event's description — which picture represents an event is the organizer's choice, and it is what the future setting is for. A third shape for stories (1080×1920) — not asked; the design object can carry a shape later. Fetching a picture from the gallery at render time — a network call inside a cached image route, and the club has not chosen a picture to fetch. Any new font or library — the card uses the Roboto and the Caveat already in the repository and `next/og`, already installed.
changelogLine: - **A prettier card to share** — the picture «Instagram» downloads and the one links show carry the club's logo, large enough to read on a phone, a deeper blue with the kit orange, the time as the headline, the route as chips and a white band with the site's address; a long title, place or tagline makes the title smaller rather than push anything off the card, and its design is one object with the platform's defaults, ready to be made the club's choice later. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 8. Given a published event, when its card is drawn in either shape, then it is drawn from one design object with platform defaults (palette, accent, which elements show, an optional tagline and background picture) that nothing stores yet; by default it carries the club's logo (150 pixels tall on the square, 100 on the wide card), the type pill as a quiet tint (a cancelled event's pill is the solid accent whether the type is shown or not, so the two differ in colour as well as in word), the title (at most three lines, cut at a word with «…» past 110 characters), the date with the time as the headline, the meeting point with a pin on one line (cut at a word with «…» past 60 characters or where its line ends), the distance and the climb as chips, and a paper band with the site's host; a switched-off element leaves no gap, and a card with a background picture keeps its white words legible under a veil — at least 4.5:1 behind the logo and the pill over a near-white photograph (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 8. Given any title, place and tagline, when the card is drawn in either shape, then every fact stays on it: the title takes the largest size at which its lines, three at most, fit the height the rest of the card leaves, so the paper band fills exactly the card's last 104 rows on the square and 80 on the wide card and the logo keeps its place; on the square a sentence-case title of up to 110 characters is drawn at 50 pixels or more (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 8. The card's background picture is fetched only from an `https:` address — never taken as a `data:` address, never through a redirect — within five seconds and four megabytes (refused on the announced length before the body is read); whatever design a caller hands over is read through `readShareCardDesign` first, and a picture that cannot be had draws the card without it (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 11. The share pictures carry the club's name as the lockup's artwork, drawn from `LOGO` in `@/theme/brand`; `CLUB_NAME` is not typed onto them, and a card whose logo is switched off names the club only through the host in its band (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 15. The share pictures carry the club's name as the lockup's artwork, drawn from `LOGO` in `@/theme/brand`, not as a typed heading read from `CLUB_NAME`, and a card with the logo off names the club only through the host (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: a prettier shared card, drawn from a design object
